item.title: Software Developer - Part Time
item.description:
Overview:

Part-time software developer at Novicell, one of Denmark’s leading digital agencies, working on the A-Team responsible for some of the country’s largest e-commerce platforms including Power.dk, Biltema.dk, and Apoteket.dk.

Key contributions:

  • Conducted a scientific feasibility study on RabbitMQ as a core messaging technology for high-throughput e-commerce platforms including Power.dk, Biltema.dk, and Apoteket.dk.
  • Designed and executed large-scale performance tests across single-node and multi-node RabbitMQ clusters, using Docker to automate deployments and ensure reproducible environments.
  • Identified a two-order-of-magnitude throughput bottleneck in the proposed production architecture, delivering findings directly to senior engineering leadership and informing revised system design.
  • Developed a dynamic, read-only C# monitoring framework for RabbitMQ, generating strongly typed models at runtime via reflection based on the server’s management API metadata.
  • Demonstrated advanced distributed-system debugging and architectural analysis skills, contributing widely referenced RabbitMQ insights on StackOverflow and briefly becoming the top-ranked contributor in the RabbitMQ tag.
  • Provided architectural guidance that helped prevent scalability issues during peak retail events and laid groundwork for future internal observability tooling.

item.title: RabbitMQ Monitoring Framework
item.description:
Overview:

During my second internship at Novicell, I identified a significant tooling gap while conducting my earlier feasibility study on RabbitMQ for high‑throughput e‑commerce workloads. Although the .NET ecosystem offered mature libraries for publishing and consuming messages, it lacked a dedicated C# framework for real‑time monitoring of RabbitMQ cluster health. Given the operational demands of Novicell’s A‑Team—responsible for platforms such as Power.dk, Biltema.dk, and Apoteket.dk—I proposed a focused project to design a lightweight, read‑only monitoring library capable of providing developers with live insights into RabbitMQ cluster metrics.

item.title: Feasibility Study of RabbitMQ
item.description:
Overview:

During my internship at Novicell, I was part of the A‑Team, the department responsible for maintaining and developing the solutions for three of Denmark’s largest e‑commerce platforms: Power.dk (a major consumer electronics retailer), Biltema.dk (one of the country’s biggest consumer goods chains), and Apoteket.dk (a large national pharmacy platform). These systems experience extreme traffic spikes during events such as Black Friday and the Christmas shopping season. To support the scalability demands of these high‑throughput environments, I was tasked with a structured, scientific investigation into whether RabbitMQ could serve as a reliable core technology for message processing and load distribution. The goal was to determine its architectural suitability and ensure that the company’s systems could handle peak seasonal workloads without service degradation.
